topic: NSAID therapy in axSpA: continuous vs on-demand, radiographic progression
synopsis: This review examines whether NSAIDs slow radiographic progression in axial spondyloarthritis rather than only relieving symptoms. Two randomized trials compared continuous with on-demand NSAID use and reached opposite conclusions. In the celecoxib trial, TNF-inhibitor-naive patients with ankylosing spondylitis were randomized to continuous versus on-demand celecoxib 100 mg twice daily or higher; after 2 years the continuous-use group had less radiographic progression (p=0.002), and a post-hoc analysis found the slowing was greater when ESR or CRP was elevated. A separate diclofenac trial did not reproduce that benefit, so the review treats a disease-modifying effect of continuous NSAIDs as uncertain.

teachingPoints.claim: Continuous celecoxib was associated with less 2-year radiographic progression than on-demand use in one trial (p=0.002).

teachingPoints.claim: The celecoxib slowing of progression was greater in patients with elevated ESR or CRP.
